title: Stock Market Today Live, Sept 15: Sensex down over 440 pts, Nifty slips below 23,280 as Crude, Fed fears drag markets into red - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Businessmen investor think before buying stock market investment using smartphone to analyze trading data. investor analysis with stock exchange graph on screen. Financial stock market. | Photo Credit: champpixs

Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates - Broad market breadth on the BSE confirmed the negative tone: of 4,513 stocks traded, 2,884 declined against 1,376 advances and 253 unchanged. There were 263 stocks in the lower circuit versus 181 in the upper circuit. The number of stocks at 52-week lows, at 156, nearly matched those at 52-week highs at 151.

Information technology stocks continued to dominate the gainers list, extending the morning’s sector rotation. HCL Technologies led the Nifty 50 with a gain of 5.68 per cent to ₹1,274.60 on volumes of 32.81 lakh shares worth ₹41,969.97 lakhs.

Brent crude trading near $107 a barrel and WTI at $102.82, up 0.92 per cent on the day, remained the dominant macro concern.

The USD/INR pair extended its recent move, testing the 95.80 resistance zone after the rupee weakened more than 1 per cent last week to close near 95.55.

The Federal Reserve’s two-day FOMC meeting, which began today, remained the single most-watched event globally. Markets are pricing a 60 per cent probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike, driven by persistent energy-led inflation and strong U.S. consumer credit data, which came in at $18.06 billion against a forecast of $11.90 billion. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield, which briefly crossed 5 per cent overnight, continued to reflect investor unease.

The Sensex had opened the session at 75,369.63 against a previous close of 74,781.76, while the Nifty opened at 23,576.15 against a previous close of 23,398.10, both indices gapping up before retreating sharply through the morning session.

Nifty declines as IT gains can't offset market losses from rising crude prices and Fed rate hike fears.

Sensex fell 242.74 pts or 0.32% to 74,539.02 at 1.13 pm, and Nifty 50 shed 98.80 pts or 0.42% to 23,299.30.

Fintech Cloud Private Limited, a technology company providing loan servicing and technology-enabled solutions to regulated financial entities, has entered into a definitive agreement with Indiabulls Limited, under which Indiabulls will acquire a 70% stake in the company at an equity valuation of ₹1,500 crore.

The proposed transaction, valued at ₹1,050 crore for the 70% stake, marks a significant milestone in Fintech Cloud’s growth journey and will bring the company into a strategic partnership with a listed financial services player. The transaction is proposed to be completed through an NCLT-approved scheme, with the consideration to be settled through the issuance of up to 21 crore fully paid-up equity shares of Indiabulls Limited, subject to applicable regulatory and pricing requirements.

Founded in January 2021, Fintech Cloud operates as a Loan Service Provider (LSP) for regulated entities and provides technology solutions to the NBFC sector. The company reported gross revenue of ₹133.77 crore and profit before tax of ₹30.31 crore in FY2025-26.

The company’s financial performance represents a significant scale-up, with the company reporting nil turnover in FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 before recording approximately ₹133.77 crore in revenue in FY2025-26.

Tata Group stocks witnessed strong buying interest on Tuesday after the RBI rejected Tata Sons’ application to deregister as a non-bank lender, reviving prospects of a stock market listing for the holding company.

Daksham Capital has appointed Saurabh Mundhra as Co-Founder & Head - West, effective August 1, 2026. Bringing over two decades of experience in corporate banking, capital markets, and strategic finance—most recently as Director at HSBC—he will lead and scale the firm’s advisory franchise in the Western region. The strategic hire aligns with Daksham’s expansion across wealth advisory, private capital, and structured solutions for promoters and family businesses. Co-Founder & Group CEO Saket Lakhotia highlighted Mundhra’s corporate finance expertise as key to deepening early-stage client engagement and supporting long-term growth strategies.

AU Small Finance Bank (AU SFB) announced on Monday the appointment of Anil Agarwal as Senior Executive Group Head, Commercial & Institutional Banking and Amol Padhye as Chief Risk Officer, as the lender prepares for its proposed transition to a Universal Bank following an RBI in-principle approval.

Citi launches eFPI @ Citi, Reducing Foreign Portfolio Investors Registration Timeline to Five Business Days

Tuhin Kanta Pandey, Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said, “We appreciate Citi’s initiative to provide faster registration timeline of 5 days for FPIs in India. It aligns with SEBI’s thrust on utilizing technology to facilitate FPIs to access Indian Capital markets expeditiously.”
